scope: Read-only review of the local provider/analyst/skeptic integration-role run
testSummary: 1 pass, 0 fail, 116 assertions; 13 scripted role scenarios

skepticalReviewer.scenario: A deterministic second pass disagreed with an optimistic supported verdict on mitigation.
skepticalReviewer.observed: The API returned insufficient_evidence after two local TLS provider calls.
skepticalReviewer.conclusion: The disagreement path abstains as intended; this says nothing about an external model's judgment quality.

overtrustingAnalyst.scenario: A deliberate false-positive provider returned supported twice for an exact claim that equipment was repaired and independent post-action measurements established sustained methane reduction. The excerpt only documents an investigation, says repair was not independently checked, and supplies no post-action measurement.
overtrustingAnalyst.observed: The exact review confirms the excerpt is sent in pass one and only the grounded quotation is sent in pass two. The API preserved a supported but unreviewed suggestion, kept it private to an unauthenticated reader, and rejected anchoring with 409 using the expected human-review error. The bundle states physical verification is not established.
overtrustingAnalyst.conclusion: The fixture demonstrates the correlated-pass limitation and checks that the result stays a suggestion behind review and anchor controls. It does not test whether a real analyst would understand the UI.

scenarios: A fabricated citation not present in the submitted excerpt caused abstention after one call.

HTTP 503, HTTP 429, redirect, invalid JSON, invalid first-pass schema, invalid second-pass schema, oversized response, and a stalled partial response all produced a generic 502, no new audit revision, and no redirect-target request.
The partial-body case took 40198 ms, satisfying the fixture's 39-48 second window and demonstrating the API's configured deadline without an earlier provider-server idle timeout.
The invalid second-pass response required two provider calls before failing closed; other provider-failure cases failed after one call.
providerAdversary.conclusion: The deterministic local HTTPS fixture exercised the real API process, TLS trust, exact per-pass payload scope, provider authorization, response parsing, and failure boundary. Prompt-injection behavior was not evaluated by a model.

roleReview.anonymousVisitor: Missing assessment authentication returned 401; missing consent and rights declarations returned 400; provider calls and audits remained at zero.
roleReview.serviceOperator: Production-mode local API accepted the configured CORS origin and did not allow an unrelated origin. The runner used flock -F to exec the API directly, canonicalized and prepared the audit path before launch, observed the API child exit, and confirmed /api/health was unreachable after SIGKILL before starting the replacement API. It kept the audit file mode at 0600 and recovered three immutable drafts from the same local path.

priorAttempts.boundary: Private-history authorization returned 401 because the fixture directory used an invalid checkedBy identifier containing a space. The fixture was corrected to a valid identifier; no application change was made.

The provider fixture's default 10-second idle timeout ended the partial response early. This was not accepted as deadline evidence; the fixture was updated to use a 60-second idle timeout and an explicit elapsed-time assertion.
Earlier 11-scenario run passed 99 assertions and measured a 40173 ms partial-body deadline; it did not yet assert exact second-pass payload contents or exact anchor error text.

Passed 116 assertions with direct flock -F API execution and a post-SIGKILL health check; the final run also added canonical audit-path preparation and readiness checks before and after health succeeds.
Passed 116 assertions with direct API crash observation; it preceded canonical audit-path preparation and child-exit checks around readiness.

Passed 116 assertions with canonical audit path and direct API crash proof, but the exact claim did not yet explicitly assert physical repair and post-action methane measurements; the final fixture strengthens that false-positive case.

externalLimits: The provider was a deterministic local HTTPS fixture; externalProviderCalls is 0. No real model, provider retention policy, accuracy, or semantic citation quality was evaluated.
The roles are scripted test perspectives, not independent AI-agent sessions or human participants.
The embedded untrusted-instruction string was sent through the deterministic fixture; the test does not establish resistance by a real model.
The API child exit and listener-down assertion establish the tested local crash boundary; they do not establish deployment lifecycle behavior.
The recorded model version is the configured alias, not a verified provider-served model identity.
Local same-volume crash recovery does not establish public-host persistence or deployment behavior.
No public deployment was verified and no Sepolia receipt was checked.
